claim: Anycast static IPs are dedicated to your AWS account and spread across geographic regions; you can allowlist them with network providers to waive data charges for viewers, or use them in outbound firewalls.
question: What are CloudFront Anycast static IPs used for?

values.display: dedicated to your AWS account
waive data charges for viewers

evidence.quote: You can request Anycast static IPs from CloudFront to use with your distributions. Anycast static IP lists can contain only IPv4 IP addresses or both IPv4 and IPv6 IP addresses. These IP addresses are dedicated to your AWS account and spread across geographic regions.

You can request 21 Anycast static IP addresses to allowlist with network providers so that you can waive data charges for viewers who access your application. Alternatively, you can use these static IPs within outbound security firewalls to control traffic exchange with approved applications. Anycast static IP lists can be used with one or more distributions.

claim: For routing an apex domain such as example.com directly to CloudFront, you request Anycast static IPs for that use case and add A records in your DNS that point the apex domain to CloudFront.
question: How can an apex domain be routed to CloudFront with Anycast static IPs?

values.display: routing of apex domains
add A records in your DNS

evidence.quote: If you want to enable routing of apex domains (such as example.com) directly to your CloudFront distributions, you can request 3 Anycast static IP addresses for this use case. Then, add A records in your DNS to point the apex domain to CloudFront.

claim: To use Anycast static IP lists with a distribution, the price class of the distribution must be Use all edge locations.
question: Which price class does a distribution need to use CloudFront Anycast static IP lists?

values.display: select Use all edge locations
Anycast static IP lists with your CloudFront distribution

evidence.quote: To use Anycast static IP lists with your CloudFront distribution, you must select **Use all edge locations** for the price class for the distribution.

claim: CloudFront continuous deployment tests a CDN configuration change on a subset of production traffic using a staging distribution and a continuous deployment policy, and the change is then promoted to the primary distribution.
question: What does CloudFront continuous deployment let you do?

values.display: testing first with a subset of production traffic
staging distribution
primary distribution

evidence.quote: With Amazon CloudFront *continuous deployment* you can safely deploy changes to your CDN configuration by testing first with a subset of production traffic.

You can use a *staging distribution* and a *continuous deployment policy* to send some traffic from real (production) viewers to the new CDN configuration and validate that it works as expected. You can monitor the performance of the new configuration in real time, and promote the new configuration to serve all traffic by using the *primary distribution* when you're ready.

claim: A multi-tenant distribution is a template that has no CloudFront routing endpoint, so it cannot be accessed directly and must be used with a connection group and one or more distribution tenants.
question: Can viewers access a CloudFront multi-tenant distribution directly?

values.display: a multi-tenant distribution cannot be accessed directly
no CloudFront routing endpoint

evidence.quote: Unlike a standard distribution, a multi-tenant distribution cannot be accessed directly because it has no CloudFront routing endpoint. Therefore, it must be used in conjunction with a connection group and one or more distribution tenants.

claim: For each new website you create a distribution tenant that inherits the settings of the multi-tenant distribution, and then you customize specific settings; each tenant supports an individual domain or subdomain.
question: How does a distribution tenant get its settings in CloudFront multi-tenant distributions?

values.display: automatically inherits the defined values of its source
supports an individual domain or subdomain

evidence.quote: For each new website, you create a distribution tenant that automatically inherits the defined values of its source distribution. Then, you customize specific settings for your distribution tenant.
The distribution tenant supports an individual domain or subdomain.

claim: CloudFront can deliver video on demand or live streaming video from any HTTP origin; an encoder must package the video into segments and manifest files first.
question: What must happen to video before CloudFront can distribute it?

values.display: video on demand (VOD) or live streaming video
use an encoder to package video content

evidence.quote: You can use CloudFront to deliver video on demand (VOD) or live streaming video by using any HTTP origin.
You must use an encoder to package video content before CloudFront can distribute the content. The packaging process creates *segments* that contain your audio, video, and captions content.

claim: For live streaming, CloudFront caches media fragments at the edge so that multiple requests for the manifest file can be combined, which reduces the load on the origin.
question: How does CloudFront reduce origin load for live streams?

values.display: cache media fragments at the edge
reduce the load on your origin server

evidence.quote: For broadcasting a live stream, you can cache media fragments at the edge, so that multiple requests for the manifest file that delivers the fragments in the right order can be combined, to reduce the load on your origin server.

claim: WebSocket functionality is automatically enabled for any CloudFront distribution; to use it, the cache behavior must forward all viewer headers or the Sec-WebSocket-Key and Sec-WebSocket-Version headers.
question: Do you need to enable WebSockets on a CloudFront distribution?

values.display: automatically enabled to work with any distribution
Sec-WebSocket-Key
Sec-WebSocket-Version

evidence.quote: WebSocket functionality is automatically enabled to work with any distribution.
Specifically forward the `Sec-WebSocket-Key` and `Sec-WebSocket-Version` request headers in your origin request policy.

claim: CloudFront supports WebSocket, a TCP-based protocol for long-lived bidirectional connections between clients and servers.
question: What is WebSocket on CloudFront used for?

values.display: TCP-based protocol
long-lived bidirectional connections between clients and servers

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudFront supports using WebSocket, a TCP-based protocol that is useful when you need long-lived bidirectional connections between clients and servers.

claim: CloudFront supports gRPC, an open-source RPC framework built on HTTP/2, and proxies gRPC requests directly to the origins.
question: Does CloudFront support gRPC?

values.display: gRPC, an open-source remote procedure call (RPC) framework built on HTTP/2
proxies them directly to your origins

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudFront supports gRPC, an open-source remote procedure call (RPC) framework built on HTTP/2.
CloudFront receives your gRPC requests and proxies them directly to your origins.

claim: To handle gRPC, a distribution must include HTTP/2 among its supported HTTP versions and allow the POST method, and the gRPC origin must support HTTPS because only end-to-end HTTPS gRPC is supported.
question: What must a distribution allow to handle gRPC requests?

values.display: include HTTP/2 as one of the supported HTTP versions
gRPC only supports end-to-end HTTPS

evidence.quote: To enable a distribution to handle gRPC requests, include HTTP/2 as one of the supported HTTP versions, and allow HTTP methods, including `POST`. Your gRPC origin endpoint must be configured to support HTTPS, as CloudFront only supports secure (HTTPS-based) gRPC connections. gRPC only supports end-to-end HTTPS.

claim: CloudFront proxies gRPC requests directly to the origin and bypasses the regional edge cache, so gRPC does not support Lambda@Edge or Origin Shield.
question: Why does gRPC not support Lambda@Edge or Origin Shield on CloudFront?

values.display: bypasses the Regional Edge Cache (REC)
gRPC doesn't support Lambda@Edge or Origin Shield

evidence.quote: CloudFront proxies gRPC requests directly to the origin and bypasses the Regional Edge Cache (REC). Because gRPC bypasses the REC, gRPC doesn't support [Lambda@Edge](lambda-at-the-edge.md) or [Origin Shield](origin-shield.md).

claim: The CloudFront control plane (the public APIs for managing distributions) is hosted in us-east-1, and the data plane is the distribution itself, served from the PoPs in the edge network.
question: Where is the CloudFront control plane hosted, and what is its data plane?

values.display: is hosted in us-east-1
the distribution itself served from the PoPs

qualifiers.scope: CloudFront control plane and data plane

evidence.quote: The Amazon CloudFront control plane consists of all public CloudFront APIs for managing distributions, and is hosted in us-east-1. The data plane is the distribution itself served from the PoPs in the edge network.

claim: During a CloudFront control plane impairment, create, update and invalidation operations may not work, but content continues to be cached and served and origin failovers continue to work.
question: What keeps working when the CloudFront control plane is impaired?

values.display: your content will continue to be cached
origin failovers

evidence.quote: During a control plane impairment, CRUDL-type operations for CloudFront (including invalidation requests) may not work, but your content will continue to be cached and served, and [origin failovers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/high_availability_origin_failover.html) will continue to work.

claim: A statically-stable CloudFront design uses automated origin failovers; manually updating the distribution configuration after an origin failure would depend on the CloudFront control plane.
question: Which CloudFront design is statically stable when an origin fails?

values.display: automated origin failovers
depend on the CloudFront control plane

evidence.quote: What this means is that when you are planning for dependencies on CloudFront, you should not rely on the CloudFront control plane in your recovery path. For example, a statically-stable design would be to use automated origin failovers to mitigate the impact from an impairment to one of your origins.
A non-statically-stable design would be to manually update the configuration of your distribution in response to an origin failure. This approach would depend on the CloudFront control plane.

claim: The AWS Global Accelerator control plane (the public APIs) is hosted in us-west-2, and the data plane is the network routing of the anycast IP addresses to your registered endpoints.
question: Where is the Global Accelerator control plane hosted?

values.display: is hosted in us-west-2
network routing of the anycast IP addresses

qualifiers.scope: Global Accelerator control plane and data plane

evidence.quote: The AGA control plane consists of all public AGA APIs and is hosted in us-west-2. The data plane is the network routing of the anycast IP addresses provided by AGA to your registered endpoints.

claim: During a Global Accelerator control plane impairment, create, update and delete operations may not work, but routing to existing endpoints and the existing health checks, traffic dials and endpoint weights continue to work.
question: What keeps working when the Global Accelerator control plane is impaired?

values.display: Routing to your existing endpoints
will continue to work

evidence.quote: During a control plane impairment, CRUDL-type operations for AGA may not work. Routing to your existing endpoints, as well as existing health checks, traffic dials, and endpoint weight configurations used to route or shift traffic to other endpoints and endpoint groups, will continue to work.

claim: A statically-stable Global Accelerator design uses the status of configured health checks to fail away from unhealthy endpoints; changing traffic dials, editing endpoint groups or removing endpoints during an impairment depends on the control plane.
question: Which Global Accelerator actions are not statically stable during an impairment?

values.display: use the status of the configured health checks
modify the AGA traffic dial percentages

evidence.quote: For example, a statically-stable design would be to use the status of the configured health checks to fail away from unhealthy endpoints.

A non-statically-stable design would be to modify the AGA traffic dial percentages, edit endpoint groups, or remove an endpoint from an endpoint group during an impairment. These approaches would depend on the AGA control plane.

claim: The CloudFront managed prefix list contains the IP ranges of the CloudFront origin-facing servers; used in a VPC security group it allows inbound traffic to your origin only from CloudFront and is maintained by CloudFront.
question: How can a security group allow only CloudFront traffic to reach an origin in AWS?

values.display: The CloudFront managed prefix list contains the IP
prevents non-CloudFront traffic from reaching your origin

evidence.quote: The CloudFront managed prefix list contains the IP address ranges of all of the CloudFront globally distributed origin-facing servers.
The prefix list allows inbound traffic to your origin only from CloudFront origin-facing servers, which prevents non-CloudFront traffic from reaching your origin.

claim: With a Route 53 alias resource record set for a CloudFront distribution you do not pay for Route 53 queries, and you can create an alias record for the root domain name (example.com), which DNS does not allow for CNAMEs.
question: How can you point a zone apex such as example.com at a CloudFront distribution?

values.display: you don’t pay for Route 53 queries
root domain name (example.com)

evidence.quote: With an alias resource record set, you don’t pay for Route 53 queries. You can also create an alias resource record set for the root domain name (example.com), which DNS doesn’t allow for CNAMEs.

claim: One-click protection in the CloudFront console creates an AWS WAF web ACL with AWS recommended rules and attaches it to the distribution for you; you can also attach a preconfigured web ACL.
question: What does CloudFront one-click AWS WAF protection do?

values.display: creates an AWS WAF web access control list
attaches the web ACL to the CloudFront distribution

evidence.quote: Use one-choose protection in the CloudFront console. One-choose protection creates an AWS WAF web access control list (web ACL), configures rules to protect your servers from common web threats, and attaches the web ACL to the CloudFront distribution for you. The topics in this section assume the use of one-choose protections.
